reconciliation_basis: Rechecked existing crate-root exports and current private observer/fault boundaries; generic dispatch/RuntimeHost move rationale does not make private CiQueries, inspection leases, raw process observers or comparator diagnostics injectable. Current admission rules require the cheapest boundary that preserves the same guarantee. The twelve old gc.rs identities resolve to the split cleanup.rs and gc/tests files; nine collector cases relocate, three final-removal safety cases retain their specific private seams. No visibility widened or production logic changed.

entries.evidence: The callback receives observed byte counts and the recent raw bytes before exit; public run_cli_backend configures tracing progress internally and accepts no callback. The existing 15-byte sample assertion needs that observer, not merely a final audit blob.

This native process-group/pipe harness applies a 150ms deadline and checks the raw prefix, absent exit code and grandchild death within the 2s return budget. The exported provider accepts whole-second activity timeouts and projects terminal envelopes; scenario_c_wall_clock_timeout proves activity timeout but does not observe this pipe-holding grandchild or raw capture.

The isolated observer asserts the effective C locale, removed LANGUAGE/GIT_CONFIG_* authority and disabled fsmonitor for every constructor/verification Git command. This security case was explicitly admitted in the current strategy on the delivery base; provider dispatch performs other Git calls and consumes the lease/verification internally, so it cannot apply the observer exclusively to this private boundary.

The fixture leases and drops an inspection handle, then corrupts precisely its slot owner or removes it while retaining the checkout; missing commits and blobs are controls. Public dispatch consumes the lease internally and does not export the slot handle/owner transition. Recreating a provider lifecycle merely to recover that slot adds a separate mechanism to this ownership refusal invariant.

The fixture retains up to 64 SourceInspection handles to force pool exhaustion, alongside blocked-pool and invalid-gitdir IO controls. Public provider dispatch owns and drops these handles internally; forcing exhaustion there needs concurrent live providers and coordinated leases, rather than the bounded deterministic handle harness.

The private constructor accepts a 500ms copy budget while the Git shim stalls for 600 seconds; a subsequent lease verifies that the failed lease cleaned the slot. Public activity timeout is not the inspection copy deadline and cannot replace this seam without waiting out the bulk production bound.

The private producer/parser pair tests Unicode title truncation with unmatched subject brackets, and parses both the subject and full message while rejecting the title body. Neither parser nor message builder is exported. A commit action can expose the message but not the parser result; reproducing parser behavior in an integration test would not test it.

The script fails only where candidate.txt exists; the private comparator exposes BasePasses and the second call exposes its cached base_log bit. The exported verify_claimed_known_red runs only the base and returns a refusal set/type, not a candidate rerun, comparator verdict or cache diagnostic. Public review settlement would add the review/task lifecycle to observe this comparator-specific fault/cache guarantee.

The isolated child observes locale through a Git alias in both text and byte runners, then plants a ref lock to assert C-locale retry classification. No public engine API executes arbitrary Git argv through both runners. Current strategy explicitly admits this security observer on the delivery base.

Silent aliases deterministically exit 37 or kill their Git parent; the fixture observes the text and byte outcome fields and diagnostic conversion for each. Public VCS operations expose prescribed argv and JSON projections, not arbitrary aliases or both raw runner outcomes. Retain the existing missing-diagnostic fault harness without exporting those runners.

The fixture verifies head/tail ordering for both capped streams, omitted UTF-8 middle, stderr diagnostic retention inside the repair reader’s 32KiB tail, and missing-tool classification. RequiredCommandRun and the runner are private. Public review/commit gates wrap the result in capped repair records and can redact/project it, hiding an earlier capture defect; they also require task/delivery validation setup for each stream shape.

The private removal entry verifies the owned checkout and branch are entirely removed even with read-only descendants. Public setup may force removal only as part of replacing a checkout and leaves a new checkout at that path; public GC refuses force except after candidate recovery. Those callers cannot expose the same terminal removal assertion without adding lifecycle behavior.

The fixture bypasses the collector’s preliminary dirty check and reaches Git’s final non-force gate on an already dirty tree. Public GC returns earlier and cannot prove that last removal gate; forcing a change after GC’s check would require a new interleaving seam. Its bytes-preserved assertion must stay at the private safety seam.

This forces permission repair on a worktree containing a symlink to a read-only outside directory and checks the outside mode remains 0555 after complete removal. Public GC’s dirty-path/candidate recovery checks precede this forced seam, and public setup recreates the checkout. The existing narrow private permission-restoration safety harness remains economical.
